claims.text: Interfacial anchoring strength is the dominant factor governing premelting and melting behavior in high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Strong metal-support interactions at defect-rich support sites limit the mobility of nanoparticle surface atoms.
Restricting surface-atom mobility delays the onset of surface premelting.
Restricting surface diffusion increases the melting temperature relative to unsupported particles.
Unsupported high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles premelt and melt at lower temperatures because their surface atoms diffuse more freely.
Fast moving bed pyrolysis can synthesize supported high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles containing five to ten elements.
Fast moving bed pyrolysis can produce supported high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles with a narrow size distribution around 2 nm.
The nanoparticles produced by fast moving bed pyrolysis have homogeneous elemental mixing.
High-entropy-alloy nanoparticles can be immobilized on granular carbon or gamma-Al2O3 supports.
A high-surface-energy granular substrate provides abundant nanoparticle anchoring sites.
Bonding to graphitic edge sites can create strong support-nanoparticle anchoring.
Supported nanoparticles will exhibit a statistically measurable delay in premelting and a higher melting point than composition- and size-matched unsupported nanoparticles.
The support-induced thermal-stability improvement will be significant and reproducible over nanoparticle sizes of approximately 2 to 10 nm.
Fast moving bed pyrolysis is a rapid, high-temperature synthesis method and has been demonstrated at 923 K for supported high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The proposed support effect applies to rapidly synthesized, supported high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles in the approximately 2 to 10 nm size range.
Weak support interactions or substantial deviations in particle size will make the support effect less pronounced or otherwise alter it.
Prior Joule-heating studies show that strong metal-support interactions enhance nanoparticle thermal stability.
The respective contributions of intrinsic high-entropy lattice distortion and interfacial stabilization have not been isolated.
